subject: Security exhibit follow-up: bounded inspection onboarding playbook
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit follow-up: bounded inspection onboarding playbook

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Attached is a working draft of our "assurance playbook" that we use to operationalize the security exhibit and audit rights in the order form. Key points up-front: we propose bounded, virtual-only inspections (no on-site unless escalated), scoped sampling rather than unlimited audits, and a staged pen-test window limited to staging with a short notice window.

Please review section 2 ("Inspection scope and sampling") and section 4 ("Pen test access & staging rules"). High-level asks for Nexera to confirm:
- Accept virtual-only inspections with a maximum of four 8-hour sessions per 12 months and sampling limited to the agreed artifact list.
- Agreement that penetration testing is executed against a staging environment we provision (isolated from production) with agreed test accounts and IP allowlist.
- 72-hour standard notice for routine inspections and 48-hour notice for pen-test windows (we are flexible on the latter if you prefer 72).

I've also attached a redline of the current order form where we propose tightened language for "audit rights" (attached as orderform_redline_Nexera_v2.docx).

Attachments: assurance_playbook_v0.3.pdf; orderform_redline_Nexera_v2.docx

Next step: if these guardrails look reasonable, can you confirm by EOD Thu 6/12 so we can loop Legal and finalize the exhibit language? If you have a standard questionnaire we should use instead of our playbook, please send it over (we can map responses).

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Head, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Ng <sara.ng@nexeralabs.com>

Cc: Tim Evans <tim.evans@medica-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit follow-up: bounded inspection onboarding playbook

Marissa —

Thanks for the draft. A few quick notes from Nexera's security team after a skim:

- We prefer 48-hour notice for both routine inspections and pen-test windows; shorter notice matters for scheduling our third-party assessor.
- We need explicit ability to engage a third-party assessor of record (we'll share assessor details and proof of insurance).
- We cannot accept any language that is interpreted as "no prior limits" on scope. The sampling approach you propose is sensible, but we will need the artifact list to include specific log types (auth logs, KMS audit entries, sysdig/host agent snapshots where available).
- SOC 2: we require the most recent Type II report and a management letter when available; frequency of handover should be 1x/year.
- Regarding pen tests: we insist on a written attestation that pen-tests will be executed in staging and that Redwood will provide a time-limited, least-privilege test account. We will also permit an on-site only in a critical incident + mutual agreement clause.

I've attached our questionnaire (nexera_questions.xlsx) and flagged a few items you might want to pre-populate.

If your Legal wants to propose specific exhibit language, send it across and I'll have our counsel review in parallel.

Best,

Sara Ng
Security Program Manager, Nexera Labs
sara.ng@nexeralabs.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Security exhibit follow-up: bounded inspection onboarding playbook

Karthik — forwarding Nexera's initial replies (below). They want 48-hour notice, third-party assessor rights, and specific log categories in the artifact list.

Can Legal review the attached order form redline and propose exhibit language that:
1) preserves our operational controls (staging-only pen tests, limited virtual sessions, proof of insurance for assessors),
2) limits audit rights to "bounded virtual inspection" with defined artifact types and sampling percentages, and
3) requires production of SOC2 Type II and management letter once per year (we can avoid sharing raw control evidence where we have contractual constraints).

We prefer to avoid open-ended on-site rights; suggest language that permits on-site only for critical incident response and with >14 days' mutually agreed notice and compensation for travel if required.

Attachments: orderform_redline_Nexera_v2.docx

Can you return marked comments by EOD Fri 6/13? I want to get an updated packet back to Sara so they can route to procurement.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security exhibit follow-up: bounded inspection onboarding playbook

Team —

Quick read and proposed approach (high level):

- Accept third-party assessors subject to (i) proof of insurance and (ii) acceptance to our NDA / rules of engagement. We will add a short "assessor onboarding" clause to the exhibit.
- Replace any language that implies unlimited "audit rights" with "bounded virtual inspection" definition: max four virtual sessions in a 12-month period, sampling capped at 2% of transactions or 5k records (whichever is lower) per session, and explicit artifact list (auth logs, KMS audit trail, network flow summaries, staging DB snapshots limited to anonymized sample sets).
- Pen-test language: require staging-only execution, with a minimum 48-hour notice and a max 72-hour allowed notice if the assessor cannot meet 48 hours. Require a scoped test plan and a short attestation post-test. Add a clause that Redwood may refuse on-site access except for incident response with 14-day mutual notice and agreed cost reimbursement.
- SOC 2: agree to provide most recent Type II report plus management letter annually; do not provide raw control evidence unless mandated by the order form for a specific control, in which case we will provide redacted evidence or a summarized control statement.

Proposed next steps: I will upload a redline of the order form with the exhibit language replaced by the above bullets (file: orderform_redline_KI_comments.docx). Laura/Vanessa, please confirm that the operational constraints (staging account provisioning, IP allowlist, artifact retention windows) are implementable — I flagged a few items in the doc where product may need to commit.

If Nexera can accept these constraints, we should be able to close the exhibit and finalize the order form. If they insist on broader rights, we will escalate via Sales for commercial tradeoffs.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
